results.reason: Alpine has no required or typed component inputs: an `Alpine.data` factory can take arguments, but nothing declares which ones a component needs or their types. This baseline's status line reads `open` through the scope Alpine shares with the component that owns it, so the page passes it no input it could leave out.

Alpine has no required or typed component inputs: an `Alpine.data` factory can take arguments, but nothing declares which ones a component needs or their types. This baseline's status line reads `open` through the scope Alpine shares with the component that owns it, so the page passes it no input it could give the wrong type.

An Alpine component nested inside another shares its parent's scope instead of receiving a copy of the parent's values. Assigning `open = false` in the status line therefore changes the parent's own `open` and closes the details correctly, so the code this mistake describes works as intended.

The card dispatches `hide` with no value (`$dispatch('hide')`). Each card sits in its own Alpine wrapper, and that wrapper's listener hides itself, so the page already knows which card the event came from and the event carries no payload whose type could be wrong.

The mistake cannot be written: HTMX sends `hx-vals` as ordinary form fields, and a form field is always text, so `hx-vals='{"amount": "1"}'` sends exactly the same request as `{"amount": 1}`. The view turns the field into a whole number with `int(request.POST['amount'])`, as it must for any form field, so the counter works.

results.reason: Jinja's reusable component is a macro, and the page fills it with a {% call %} block that the macro inserts with caller(). A call block fills one unnamed region, so the page has no footer name to misspell. Jinja's named blocks belong to template inheritance, which Jinja's docs use for page layouts; for repeated markup they present macros. A misspelled macro name is m01 and a misspelled argument name is m02.

Alpine does not render components on the server: in the browser it runs on the HTML the server sent and overwrites x-text content without comparing it to the server's text. Nothing renders the same component on both sides, so there is no mismatch for any tool to report.

Starlette's docs cover no translations, and its Jinja2Templates creates a Jinja Environment with no extensions. Jinja's i18n extension works only after the developer adds it and installs gettext translations, which this stack's standard setup does not do, so the heading is literal text and there is no message key to misspell.

results.reason: In JavaScript the API base `/api` is a plain string: the language has no path type, and its URL class needs a full address or a base address to resolve against, which a relative setting like `/api` does not have, so a developer would not wrap it in one. A set or a date is not a natural type for an API base. The server component hands the client component the same string value the browser code renders.
